bridge: Builds on R01/R02 and all required foundation/assessment topics. Choose a specialty for further depth; this project is a foundation capstone, not an accredited degree or a claim of PhD-level novelty.
teaching:
A capstone integrates explanation, implementation or analysis, verification and communication. Define a bounded question with deliverables another person can inspect. “Master cybersecurity” is a long-term ambition; a reviewable project needs a smaller claim and explicit acceptance criteria.

Use the provided synthetic detection project as a complete baseline option. Preserve its dataset, version rules and calculate results without leaking evaluation labels into the rule. Discuss costs and visibility limits. To pursue research later, identify an open question relative to existing work, secure appropriate mentorship and evidence, and subject novelty claims to specialist review.

A reviewer should check the artifact and your reasoning, not only a progress percentage. Submit a report, reproducible inputs/code or hand calculations, test cases, limitations and a short oral defence. Independent certification exams have their own eligibility and assessment standards; completing this hub does not automatically award an external credential.

State exactly what your assurance evidence establishes. A test demonstrates behaviour for its executed cases and environment; a clean run does not establish all possible behaviours. A proof establishes a property of a specified model under explicit assumptions. For example, \(\{x\geq0\}\; y:=x+1\;\{y>x\}\) holds for mathematical integers, but a fixed-width implementation needs an overflow condition or a different arithmetic model. Soundness means that the conclusions an analysis reports as guaranteed are valid under its model; completeness concerns whether it can establish every property in its stated scope. Some tools deliberately trade guarantees for useful bug finding. Record versions, build settings, dependencies and assumptions with your evidence so someone can reproduce and challenge it. Keep operational monitoring and response in the assurance case: a change or incident can invalidate yesterday’s assumptions.
example:
Capstone option: detection rule study using D07's six rows
Rule A: alerts1,2,3
Rule B: alerts1,2,3,4,5
Ground truth incidents:1,2,4; benign:3,5,6
Deliverables: dataset manifest, versioned rules, matrix/metrics,
telemetry contract, missing-field analysis, decision memo and recovery plan.
Research claim limited to this fixed synthetic test set.
explanation: A has precision/recall2/3; B has precision60% and recall100%. Those exact results are already known, so reproducing them is a learning artifact rather than a novel research contribution. The independent work is explaining tradeoffs, detecting misleading methodology and defending the limits.
exercise: Complete the supplied synthetic detection project with hand calculations or an inspected local script, not a new live evaluation. Score each area 0=missing/wrong, 1=mostly correct with an identified repairable gap, 2=complete and supported: correctness (all matrices/metrics); reproducibility (exact data/rules/steps); threat/telemetry assumptions (fields, missingness and claim limits); fair comparison (same complete cases and declared costs); communication (clear decision and limitations). Require at least 1 in every area and explain each score with evidence. Ask the other learner to identify one weakness, or conduct a separate self-review before revision.
solution: Rule A: TP=2, FP=1, FN=1, TN=2, precision/recall 2/3. Rule B: TP=3, FP=2, FN=0, TN=1, precision 3/5=60%, recall 1=100%. Keep the same six rows for both and keep truth labels out of rule inputs. A complete submission includes exact rule alert sets, dataset, calculations, telemetry/missing-field assumptions, a stated false-positive/miss cost preference, limitations and the requested response/recovery plan. For example, a correct matrix with no saved inputs might earn correctness 2 and reproducibility 0; it needs revision before completion. These marks organise review, not certify operational mastery or research novelty.
challenge: Defend the project without the walkthrough. Add a missing signal field to row 2, explain uncertainty, compare both rules under an explicit cost preference and propose a genuinely new question that would require additional data. Separate self-study completion, external certification and research degree routes.
challenge_solution: The defence preserves the missing-data limitation, justifies costs and avoids claiming broad detection mastery from six rows. A new empirical claim requires an authorised data/validation plan. External exams and university degrees are awarded by their respective bodies, not by this site.
